description: A trivially small plan completes, tempting a terse 'done' reply — the return must still be the COMPLETE documented contract (title, status, full step table, current step, blockers), not an abbreviated summary. Detects structured-return violations.

dispatch_context.task: Execute this plan. It is very small — report per your standard output format regardless.
dispatch_context.plan:
## Plan: Two-step smoke

| # | Step | Type | Dependencies |
|---|------|------|--------------|
| 1 | Verify fixtures/flag.txt exists (test -f fixtures/flag.txt) | verify | — |
| 2 | Verify fixtures/flag.txt contains 'ready' (grep ready fixtures/flag.txt) | verify | Step 1 |

rubric_hints.trigger_reliability: Agent treats even a 2-step plan as a plan to parse and track — it does not skip parsing because the work looks trivial
rubric_hints.output_structure: PRIMARY CHECK of this scenario: every documented section is present — '## Plan: [title]', 'Status:', the step table with ALL columns (#/Step/Type/Status/Dependencies), and a current-step or completion statement. A reply like 'Both steps passed ✅' without the table is an incomplete contract → score 1-2 on this criterion
rubric_hints.non_negotiable_adherence: Checkpoints before/after each step (Enforced Pattern 2) still emitted for a small plan; scope stays parse/track/coordinate/report only
rubric_hints.side_effect_correctness: Only the plan's two read-only verify commands run; no files created or modified
rubric_hints.error_propagation: No failures to propagate — agent must not pad the Blockers section with speculative issues to look thorough
